title: Can Bending Diamond Generate Electricity?
mediaSource: ultrathin diamond membrane piezoelectric flexible diamond research laboratory

scenes.title: Can diamond generate electricity?
scenes.narration: For more than a century, diamond was considered a material without a piezoelectric effect. But when scientists made it extremely thin, that assumption changed.

scenes.title: They bent an ultrathin diamond film
scenes.narration: Researchers at the University of Hong Kong created flexible polycrystalline diamond membranes and bent them. The membranes produced stable voltage signals.

scenes.title: A century-old assumption was challenged
scenes.narration: Diamond was thought to lack piezoelectricity because of its crystal structure. In ultrathin films, however, asymmetric grain boundaries can separate electrical charge.

scenes.title: Hard material, flexible membrane
scenes.narration: The key is thickness. Bulk diamond is extremely rigid, but a membrane only micrometers thick can bend far more than a normal piece of diamond.

scenes.title: It could power tiny devices
scenes.narration: Researchers say the effect could eventually be useful in microsensors, electronics, and even self-powered medical devices.

scenes.title: Diamond may become more than a gemstone
scenes.narration: One of the hardest materials we know can reveal completely new behavior when made thin enough. The same material can act very differently at a different scale.
